options: A firewall rule that only applies to the Public profile
A documented, tested set of configuration settings representing a minimum acceptable security posture
A single antivirus signature file
A vague sense of what settings seem secure
questions.explain: A baseline is specific and documented — a concrete, testable list of settings, not a general impression of security.

questions.q: What does the Microsoft Security Compliance Toolkit (SCT) provide?
options: A tool that only works on Linux servers
A replacement for Windows Firewall
A cloud-only service with no downloadable components
Version-specific Windows security baselines delivered as importable GPO backups
questions.explain: The SCT ships Microsoft's recommended baselines for specific Windows versions as GPO backups an admin can import and link.

questions.q: What makes the CIS Benchmarks different from a vendor's own baseline?
options: They are identical to the Microsoft SCT baselines
They're developed through an independent, consensus-based process and cover many platforms beyond just one vendor's products
They only apply to cloud platforms, never on-premises systems
They are written exclusively by Microsoft
questions.explain: CIS Benchmarks come from the vendor-independent Center for Internet Security through industry consensus, covering Windows, Linux, cloud platforms, and more.

questions.q: What is the general difference between CIS Benchmark Level 1 and Level 2?
options: There is no practical difference between the two levels
Level 1 is for Linux only; Level 2 is for Windows only
Level 2 is always less secure than Level 1
Level 1 is basic hardening with minimal functional impact; Level 2 is stricter hardening that can affect compatibility, for higher-security environments
questions.explain: Level 1 aims for broad compatibility with meaningful hardening; Level 2 goes further into defense-in-depth settings that may impact usability.

questions.q: Why do organizations typically start from a published baseline instead of configuring every security setting from scratch?
options: Baselines require no further customization ever
Baselines are already tested, applying them is fast and repeatable, and they give a defensible, checkable answer during an audit
Custom configuration is always more secure than any baseline
It's the only way Windows will boot
questions.explain: Starting from a tested baseline reduces human error, speeds up configuration, and gives auditors a concrete standard to check against.
